title: After jokes on GBH, state senator says agritourism like corn mazes are serious business
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Massachusetts lawmakers included a $5 million agritourism amendment in an economic development bill, supporting activities like corn mazes.
State Senator Jo Comerford criticized GBH hosts for joking about agritourism, highlighting financial challenges faced by Massachusetts farmers.
Despite jokes, the agritourism amendment passed; conference committee works on finalizing the broader economic development bill.

title: Red Sox trade Marcelo Mayer to Giants for reliever Erik Miller
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The Red Sox traded shortstop Marcelo Mayer to the Giants for reliever Erik Miller and minor league outfielder Carlos Gutierrez.
Mayer, a former top prospect, struggled with injuries and performance, playing 114 games and batting .223 for Boston.
Erik Miller, a 28-year-old lefty reliever, boasts a 2.76 ERA and powerful fastball, enhancing Boston's bullpen through 2029.

title: Patriots sign former Giants defensive tackle Casey Rogers
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: The New England Patriots signed defensive tackle Casey Rogers, previously with the Giants' practice squad.
Rogers played 10 games with the UFL's DC Defenders, recording 21 tackles and 1.5 sacks.
The Patriots' defensive line includes Milton Williams, Christian Barmore, and others, with Rogers now practicing in Foxborough.

title: 5 things to know about new Red Sox catcher Adley Rutschman
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The Red Sox acquired catcher Adley Rutschman from the Orioles, trading Carlos Narvaez and four prospects, including Anthony Eyanson and Kyson Witherspoon.
Rutschman, drafted first overall in 2019, has been limited to 67 games this season due to injuries, batting .251 with eight homers.
Rutschman set an MLB record at Fenway Park in 2023, becoming the first catcher to record five hits and four RBIs on Opening Day.

title: 5 takeaways from Day 8 of Patriots training camp
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: A.J. Brown continued his strong performance despite dislocating his thumb, completing practice after taping it up.
Efton Chism stood out with multiple touchdowns during scrimmages, while Mack Hollins and Kayshon Boutte joined the second team.
Undrafted cornerback Channing Canada made notable plays, including pass breakups and nearly intercepting a pass in practice.

title: Ballot Brief: Your guide to the 2026 midterms
author: Zipporah Osei
bullets: The 2026 Massachusetts midterms include races such as the governor's race, U.S. Senate, and nine statewide ballot questions.
Early voting for the Massachusetts primaries begins on August 22, with primary elections scheduled for September 1.
Boston.com's Ballot Brief newsletter covers key debates, ballot question explainers, and essential election updates for Massachusetts voters.

title: Somerville man accused of World Cup ticket scam that netted $14K
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Robert Whelan of Somerville charged with larceny and forgery for allegedly selling fake World Cup tickets.
Whelan allegedly netted over $14,000 by falsely claiming priority World Cup ticket access due to Patriots affiliation.
Bail set at $250; court prohibits contact with victims; next court date scheduled for September 23.

title: Man charged with kidnapping, raping door-to-door salesperson in Everett
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: James Mugford, 67, of Everett, charged with kidnapping and raping a door-to-door salesperson at his Fremont Avenue home.
The assault occurred when the victim, selling phone plans, knocked on Mugford's door and was allegedly held at gunpoint.
Mugford arraigned on July 23 for aggravated rape, assault, and kidnapping; held without bail, next court date August 28.

title: Red Sox acquire catcher Adley Rutschman from Orioles
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The Red Sox acquired Adley Rutschman, Jake Rogers, and cash from the Orioles for Carlos Narvaez and three prospects.
Rutschman, a three-time All-Star, offers Boston a significant upgrade at catcher despite recent injury limitations.
Rutschman has a .251/.331/.433 slash line with eight homers in 67 games this season, under contract through 2027.

title: The top four fall foliage destinations in the U.S. are not in New England, according to Priceline
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Priceline compiled a fall foliage list from hotel searches, showing New England towns ranking lower than expected in 2026.
The Adirondacks in New York claimed the top spot, while the Berkshires, Massachusetts, ranked eighth on the list.
Bretton Woods, N.H., previously in the top three, ranked fifth this year behind four non-New England destinations.
